Corporate Architecture

The structural gateway of the IJIDI Ecosystem.

The Foundation is our dedicated civic vehicle — kept structurally separate from IJIDI Group's commercial work, so that programme funding and business activity never share one ledger.

"Trust cannot survive inside closed rooms. It demands structural consistency, honest tracking, and alignment with the people we serve — including telling people what isn't finished yet."
No mixed funds
Donor and grant money never touches commercial revenue — separate accounts, separate books.
Independent oversight
The Foundation answers for its own programmes and its own ledger, not the Group's.
Scope, Phase I
Nigeria — a Pan-African mandate for what follows once Phase I is proven.
Parent ecosystem
IJIDI Group · IJIDI Foundation · Personal Brand Hub
Strategic Allocation

The five core instruments.

Every programme we run is mapped to one of five pillars, so allocation and review stay legible from the outside.

01

Human Registration & Protection

Formal beneficiary registration and identity verification for displaced and vulnerable households.

02

Ecological Resilience

Planned local mitigation work for communities facing environmental pressure — still building programme partners.

03

Education & Economic Inclusion

Structured schooling access and future micro-grant support for households rebuilding livelihood.

04

Institutional Stability

Working with local structures to keep registration and resource distribution transparent and dispute-resistant.

05

Global Cohesion

Building verified relationships with technical and institutional partners who want field-tested programmes, not press releases.

Integrity
Governance decisions are recorded and made available to partners on request.
Disclosure
Funding sources and allocation are published, not summarised into vague totals.
Continuity
Programmes are designed to outlast any single funder, cycle, or administration.
Theory of Change

How a naira becomes a measurable outcome.

Input

Output

Outcome

Shifted condition

Livelihood and stability indicators move, and we say by how much.

Impact

Institutional trust

Communities and partners can audit the chain themselves, end to end.

Field Evidence

What is actually running right now.

Operational Phase I (Nigeria): standardizing registration and education delivery in Bama and Maiduguri, Borno State, before any wider replication.

Pillar 01 — People

Beneficiary Registration & Relief Enrollment

Households queue at branded registration tables where our field team logs identity details, records household size and immediate needs, and issues a paper record alongside a digital copy — the same record referenced in the governance ledger below. Caregivers with young children are prioritized in the queue.

Field registration active — Bama & Maiduguri, since 2022
Pillar 03 — Prosperity

School Access Programme

Registered beneficiary children placed into uniform and enrolled in partner schools, tracked from enrollment through term attendance.

Cohort enrolled
Pillar 03 — Prosperity

Micro-Grant Framework

Small working-capital grants for household income recovery, currently in structuring ahead of a pilot cohort.

Structuring phase
